content: Apply phenylephrine/witch hazel gel externally to the hemorrhoidal area after ensuring it is clean and dry. The gel may be applied up to four times daily, particularly at night, in the morning, or after bowel movements that may aggravate hemorrhoids. When using the product for the first time, puncture the foil seal with the top end of the tube’s cap. For individuals under 12 years of age, the use of this product should be determined based on the patient’s condition and whether the potential benefits outweigh the risks. For individuals aged 12 years or older, the gel should be applied externally to the clean, dry hemorrhoidal area, following the same frequency and timing guidelines as mentioned above. There are no reported adverse reactions associated with the use of this product. However, if ingested, witch hazel may cause nausea, vomiting, or liver damage. This product should not be used by individuals with hypersensitivity to phenylephrine, witch hazel, or any inactive components. It is intended for external use only and should not be used orally. Caution is advised for individuals with heart disease, hypertension, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, or prostatic hypertrophy due to the presence of phenylephrine. Discontinue use and consult a physician if hemorrhoids worsen or fail to improve within seven days. Additionally, stop using the product if symptoms such as bleeding, allergic reactions, redness, irritation, swelling, pain, or other adverse effects develop or worsen. The product should not be inserted into the rectum using a mechanical device or fingers. Pregnancy Category C: The safety of this product during pregnancy has not been established, and it is unknown whether it is excreted in breast milk. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using over-the-counter medications.
